liam: FYI hitting a weird failure mode on inference-edge-usw around 23:04 UTC — a subset of pods can't reach model-infer headless service endpoints, 502s from client side.

sana: saw the spike in SLO alerts, digging into kube-proxy logs now.

liam: k8s events look normal, endpointslice exists but some nodes resolve different IP sets depending on which node you query. feels like egress/NAT consistency issue.

maria: can you paste the endpointslice output?

liam: ```
kubectl -n infer get endpointslice model-infer -o wide
NAME               ENDPOINTS   PORTS
model-infer-56k2   3/3         8080
# but on node-a lookup we get IPs: 10.10.12.5,10.10.12.6
# on node-b lookup we get: 10.10.12.5 only
```

kai: also saw kube-proxy conntrack overflow on the same nodes in the Egress logs. NAT gateway rotated ephemeral public IPs during the incident window.

infra-bot: [incident] NAT rotation detected in us-west-edge (start: 2026-02-13T22:58:10Z). Notified network team.

liam: hypothesis: ephemeral egress IP churn + provider-side NAT affinity rules caused source IP changes -> backend saw new flows and kube-proxy conntrack entries didn't age out quickly -> asymmetric return path for headless endpoints.

sana: quick test: curl from node-a to pod IP that "disappeared" for node-b; connection hangs. tcpdump shows SYN->SYN-ACK but ACK lost when coming back through different NAT IP.

maria: interesting. endpoint slices TTL is default 0 (no TTL). controller should reconcile but if kube-proxy holds stale rules / conntrack sticky entries traffic may still be DNATed wrong.

liam: workaround applied: drained and rebooted kube-proxy on 4 affected nodes -> immediate drop in 502s.

kai: rolled conntrack flush on those nodes as well: `sudo conntrack -D -s 10.10.12.0/24`

sana: can we make this safer? two ideas: set Egress NAT to preserve source (static IPs for that pool) OR add EndpointSlice status TTL so controller re-evaluates quicker after NAT changes.

maria: also adding a kube-proxy rolling restart playbook for NAT-change events. Not ideal but pragmatic.

liam: I opened a ticket with provider to avoid ephemeral rotation during maintenance windows for us-west-edge.

deploy-bot: scheduled playbook run: `infra playbooks/kube-proxy-rollout --targets=usw-edge-affected` (ETA 00:15 UTC).

kai: long-term: consider implementing NAT stickiness tests in chaos harness (simulate NAT IP rotate and verify connectivity across headless services).

maria: agreed. I'll raise a PR to add endpointslice health probes + a controller config to reduce reconciliation interval for our headless services that drive low-latency model RPCs.

liam: closing loop: immediate mitigation = static egress IP allocation for model-infer traffic + conntrack playbook. Follow-ups: endpointslice tuning + chaos test. Thanks all :thumbsup:
